title: MoMo -the blood taker-
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Burned-out Tokyo detective Keiji Mikogami investigates murders in which victims are torn apart and drained of blood, crimes like the killing of the woman he loved ten years ago. He is saved from a vampire by Momo, who looks like a little girl but is centuries old, and is pulled into a conspiracy of monsters as he pursues revenge (Seven Seas blurb via AniList; Otaku USA review).
life_message: Grief and the hunt for justice drive the hero, but the story weighs what revenge costs.

content.note: 'A lot of blood and gore'; a couple chopped up and arranged on a table (Otaku USA; MU Blood and Gore; AniList Gore).
Grotesque multi-headed vampires, serial killer (review; MU Body Horror, Serial Killer/s).
'Some casual nudity'; an 'uncomfortable' bond between a 38-year-old man and a centuries-old vampire who looks like a child (review; MU Age Gap). No sexual relationship noted (to verify).
Gritty noir detective; not rated in sources (to verify).
Grief over a murdered lover; washed-up detective (blurb; MU Death of Loved One/s).

dominant: Revenge and justice; vampire horror; grief

frames.aligns: Mikogami seeks justice for innocent victims.
frames.concerns: Revenge as motive; gore; childlike vampire and nudity.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Mikogami vows personal revenge for his wife (blurb; review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: A washed-up cop acting outside channels (blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to a lost loved one drives him (blurb).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Momo treats the older detective as a child, flipping rank (review).

folkways.japan: A Tokyo police procedural crossed with Western vampire lore; the lone detective trope is common in Japanese noir.

delivery.evidence: Otaku USA review is descriptive and calls it gritty horror, no moralizing.
delivery.note: Revenge drives the plot without commentary in the review opened.

winners_losers: Sympathy rests with Mikogami's grief and Momo's help; vampire killers are monsters.
